name: json-small
algorithm: The json row's parse, serialise, reparse and walk on small documents: each line of the 50 MB generated JSON (one record per line, the array's punctuation cut off) is one document (312,017 lines of 75 to 661 bytes, 159 on average), its trees freed before the next; rounds times (README.md).

skip.rust: no std JSON in Rust (serde_json is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; parsing has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum is taken over the reparsed values (B18), not the serialised bytes, which differ by library (key order, escapes, number spelling)
notes: Libraries named: mk json.Parse and Value.Format, a sub-arena per round reset after each document; zig std.json.parseFromSliceLeaky and Stringify.valueAlloc, an ArenaAllocator reset after each document; go json.Decoder (UseNumber) and json.Marshal, garbage collected; cs System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse and Utf8JsonWriter, each JsonDocument disposed after each document.

The go cell keeps the json row's json.Decoder with UseNumber (numbers stay text, as in Mk), which costs a Decoder and a bytes.Reader per decode; json.Unmarshal, Go's usual call for a []byte in memory, has no UseNumber and parses numbers to float64. Same checksum either way; the allocation counts are in the README; neither is timed. The coordinator ruled (M9 batch 3, 2026-11-15) to keep the Decoder, for parity with the json row.
The input is the json row's file (the same data spec); each of its lines is one document, so no tools/bench gen option was added.

Written by lane L4b of M9 item 11.22, the Mk side from doc/reference.md and the json row's Mk program, the twins by the same agent (programme section 16 asked for different agents; the coordinator's question). Publish size unsized until the coordinator's verify -publish-size.
